note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, session time and indoor-or-outdoor answer below comes from two City of Tampa pages: the pickleball page, a grid of cards dated "Updated: 10/28/2025", and the recreation-centres list, which gives each community centre an address, a phone number and a "Features:" line. Where the City stays silent, on lighting, on price, on surface, on hours at most parks, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
The City of Tampa publishes nothing about parking at any of the sixteen venues on this page. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, and the recreation-centres page gives each centre a phone number and a "Features:" line without mentioning a lot. Restrooms are not mentioned either.

Twelve of the sixteen venues are parks or a pavilion listed under "Outdoor Pickleball". The other four are community centres whose courts are indoors and open only at the session times the City prints, so at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt, Loretta Ingraham and Port Tampa the phone number matters more than the lot.
slots.peak_hours:
Tampa states hours for two of its twelve outdoor venues and for the pavilion. Madison Street Park and Vila Brothers Park are "Open daily from sunrise to sunset". The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints "Monday-Friday, 4:30-9 pm / Saturday-Sunday, 8 am-9 pm", the only outdoor hours in the city that run to a clock time. Cuscaden Park carries the one scheduled outdoor session the City publishes, "Senior open play Wed 9-11 am". Al Barnes, Copeland, Davis Islands, Forest Hills, Highland Pines, Julian B Lane, Macfarlane and Skyview have no stated hours.

Indoors, every venue comes with a session schedule. Barksdale runs Monday 1-3 pm with free beginner lessons, then 3-5:30 pm, and Tuesday to Friday 2-5:30 pm. Forest Hills runs Monday 10 am-12:30 pm, Wednesday 10 am-1 pm and Friday 6-7:30 pm. Loretta Ingraham runs Monday and Friday 6:30-8:30 pm until summer camp begins, then Mondays only from June 2. Cordelia B Hunt runs Tuesday and Thursday evenings in two versions split at June 1. Port Tampa runs Tuesday and Thursday 6-9 pm. None of those dates carries a year, so ring the centre first.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Tampa. No card says asphalt, concrete, acrylic or cushioned, and the recreation-centres page does not describe floors.

What every card does distinguish is indoor from outdoor. Two outdoor cards also say something about what is underfoot. Davis Islands has "2 multi-purpose courts", so the court may be lined or set up for something else when you arrive. Julian B Lane Riverfront Park has "2 permanent courts" and "4 portable net courts". Every other outdoor card just says courts, and this site does not read dedicated into that. Port Tampa's court was, on the City's page, "closed for repairs through June 1", the only statement about a court's condition anywhere in the city.
slots.local_scene:
Fifty-two verified courts across sixteen venues, forty-five outdoors and seven inside community-centre buildings, all counted on a single City page dated 28 October 2025. Macfarlane Park's eight is the largest published set; Cuscaden Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park hold six each; five venues hold four; the rest hold one or two. Tampa is the second Florida city on this site after Cape Coral and the first in Hillsborough County. It also has more published indoor venues than any city here except Wichita, which is why Tampa has an indoor page.

Three venues the City lists are not published. Rowlett Park has "8 courts" at "2401 E Yukon St.", an address neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Foster Park has two courts at "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611", which the Census geocoder answers as North Clark Avenue in 33614. The Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex has two indoor courts and two City house numbers, 220 and 2200 N Oregon Ave, and the count-bearing one resolves to 33606 while the City prints 33607.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Macfarlane Park has eight outdoor pickleball courts on the City's card, the largest published set in Tampa. Rowlett Park's eight are not published because its address resolves nowhere. Eight courts is enough for a rotation to form and keep moving, which makes this the venue where turning up without a group is the most reasonable plan. The City states no hours, lighting, price or surface.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a court outside and one under a roof
best_for.text: Forest Hills has two outdoor courts and two indoor courts at one address, 724 W 109th Ave, on two City cards. The indoor pair runs to a schedule (Monday 10 am-12:30 pm, Wednesday 10 am-1 pm, Friday 6-7:30 pm) with "Play resumes after Summer Camp ends" printed beside it. The centre has a gymnasium and a phone number, 813-931-2105, on the City's recreation-centres list.

best_for.heading: Best if you want hours the City has actually written down
best_for.text: The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints hours on its card, "Monday-Friday, 4:30-9 pm / Saturday-Sunday, 8 am-9 pm", and no other Tampa outdoor venue gives a closing time later than sunset. Four courts, labelled outdoor by the City, at the same address as the New Tampa Recreation Center, 813-975-2794. Whether the evening hours are lit is not stated; this site does not infer it from the clock.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Tampa have?
faqs.a: Fifty-two are verified across sixteen City venues: 45 outdoor and 7 indoor. Macfarlane Park holds the largest published set, eight.

The City does not say, for any venue. Not one of the sixteen cards mentions lighting, so every Tampa venue is recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit. The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints hours to 9 pm without mentioning lights.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Tampa?
faqs.a: Yes, seven, in five community centres under the City's own "Indoor Pickleball" heading: two at Forest Hills, two at Loretta Ingraham, and one each at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt and Port Tampa. Each comes with a session schedule rather than open hours.

sources.evidence: The sixteen published addresses were matched at house-number level and placed in Hillsborough County, FL, inside the incorporated place Tampa. Ten resolved through the Census address file as the City writes them. Four resolved through OpenStreetMap: Al Barnes Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park because the Census file holds no record of the address, Madison Street Park because the Census dropped the East from "1224 E Madison St", and Cordelia B Hunt Center because the Census answered "4602 N Himes Ave" with "4602 S HIMES AVE, 33611". Highland Pines Park and Skyview Park stand on Census answers that change the City's street type or drop its direction, because OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the address as written. "2401 E Yukon St." (Rowlett Park) is found by neither resolver; "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611" (Foster Park) is answered by the Census as "4700 N CLARK AVE, 33614" and not found by OpenStreetMap; "220 N Oregon Ave." (Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex) resolves in 33606 against the City's 33607. Snapshot: data/sources/tampa-county-census.json
